messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: False convergence?
parts:
While creating some numerical examples for illustration, I stumbled upon a strange case:

library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-11
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.

dat_cov <-
  structure(c(1.32500270874737, 0.504176370852559, 0.213499406558664,
              -0.0632368897769514, 0.504176370852559, 1.16150418811817, 0.410940167030766,
              0.25233109019432, 0.213499406558664, 0.410940167030766, 0.999612112848533,
              0.218777130133126, -0.0632368897769514, 0.25233109019432, 0.218777130133126,
              0.889965312158214),
              dim = c(4L, 4L), dimnames = list(c("x", "m1", "m2", "y"),
                                              c("x", "m1", "m2", "y")))
# Fit a serial-mediation model
mod <-
'
m1 ~ a*x
m2 ~ b1*m1
y ~ b2*m2
indirect := a * b1 * b2
'

fit <- sem(model = mod, sample.cov = dat_cov, sample.nobs = 100, fixed.x = FALSE)
coef(fit)
#>      a     b1     b2 m1~~m1 m2~~m2   y~~y   x~~x
#>  0.381  0.354  0.219  0.960  0.846  0.834  1.312

Nothing special above. Just a serial mediation model with two mediators and no direct effect. I explored the option to fix the user-defined parameter, indirect, to a value:

# Fix the indirect effect to a small value
mod2 <-
'
m1 ~ a*x
m2 ~ b1*m1
y ~ b2*m2
indirect := a * b1 * b2
indirect == 0.006
'
fit2 <- sem(model = mod2, sample.cov = dat_cov, sample.nobs = 100, fixed.x = FALSE)
coef(fit2)
#>      a     b1     b2 m1~~m1 m2~~m2   y~~y   x~~x
#>  0.458 -0.099 -0.132  0.968  1.082  0.955  1.312
parameterEstimates(fit2)[8, ]
#>        lhs op     rhs    label   est se  z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 8 indirect := a*b1*b2 indirect 0.006 NA NA     NA       NA       NA

Nothing unusual again. The indirect effect is correctly fixed to the value (.006).
I then tried to see whether the solution is sensitive to the starting values. I set the starting values to .8 of the estimates without constraint:

fit3 <- sem(model = mod2, sample.cov = dat_cov, sample.nobs = 100, fixed.x = FALSE,
            start = coef(fit) * .8)
#> Warning in lavaan::lavaan(model = mod2, sample.cov = dat_cov, sample.nobs =
#> 100, : lavaan WARNING: estimation of the baseline model failed.
coef(fit3)
#>      a     b1     b2 m1~~m1 m2~~m2   y~~y   x~~x
#>  0.361  0.332  0.050  0.960  0.846  0.862  1.312
parameterEstimates(fit3)[8, ]
#>        lhs op     rhs    label   est se  z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 8 indirect := a*b1*b2 indirect 0.006  0 NA     NA    0.006    0.006

Again, the indirect effect is fixed to .006 as expected. (I think the warning above can be ignored because it is about the baseline model, which is relevant only when we compute incremental fix indices such as CFI.)

However, the parameter estimates are very different.

comp <- cbind(parameterEstimates(fit2)[, 1:4],
              fit2.est = formatC(parameterEstimates(fit2)$est, digits = 3, format = "f"),
              fit3.est = formatC(parameterEstimates(fit3)$est, digits = 3, format = "f"))
comp
#>        lhs op     rhs    label fit2.est fit3.est
#> 1       m1  ~       x        a    0.458    0.361
#> 2       m2  ~      m1       b1   -0.099    0.332
#> 3        y  ~      m2       b2   -0.132    0.050
#> 4       m1 ~~      m1             0.968    0.960
#> 5       m2 ~~      m2             1.082    0.846
#> 6        y ~~       y             0.955    0.862
#> 7        x ~~       x             1.312    1.312
#> 8 indirect := a*b1*b2 indirect    0.006    0.006

Moreover, it seems that fit3 should be the preferred solution because its fmin is smaller than fit2:

fitMeasures(fit2, c("fmin", "chisq", "pvalue"))
#>   fmin  chisq pvalue
#>  0.230 45.992  0.000
fitMeasures(fit3, c("fmin", "chisq", "pvalue"))
#>   fmin  chisq pvalue
#>  0.052 10.364  0.035

Is there any information available from functions like lavInspect() that may hint us that we should try other starting values? If the data is real data, we may just stop at fit2 and report the results.

-- Shu Fai

P.S.: The phenomenon above seems to be restricted to a very small range of values to which the indirect effect is fixed to. Nevertheless, I think what matters in this case is not which value we fix the indirect effect to.

messages.subject: Re: False convergence?
parts:
A quick follow-up. The problem goes away if start is set to "simple". The default value is "default".

However, routinely setting start to "simple" is not a good option because it may introduce problems in other cases.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: False convergence?
parts:
On 6/14/22 07:34, Shu Fai Cheung wrote:
> Is there any information available from functions like lavInspect() that
> may hint us that we should try other starting values?

I am afraid not. Your model contained a nonlinear equality constraint,
and optimization is just much more fragile in this case. Refitting with
different starting values is always a good idea in these settings.

Yves.

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: False convergence?
parts:
Thanks for your quick advice.

Not sure if this is useful. I sometimes use OpenMx. It has the fucntion mxTryHard() which will fit a model several times with randomly perturbed starting values. Maybe a similar function can be developed for lavaan? This is a draft one to illustrate the idea:

try_more <- function(object, attempts = 3, seed = NULL, rmin = .5, rmax = 1) {
    set.seed(seed)
    ptable <- lavaan::parameterTable(object)
    i_free <- ptable$free > 0
    i_free_p <- i_free & (ptable$op != "~~")
    k <- sum(i_free_p)
    ptable$est <- ptable$start
    x <- replicate(attempts, stats::runif(k, rmin, rmax), simplify = FALSE)
    out0 <- lapply(x, function(x) {
                      ptable_i <- ptable
                      ptable_i[i_free_p, "est"] <- ptable[i_free_p, "est"] * x
                      # Should do something to reject "bad" starting values
                      stats::update(object, start = ptable_i,
                                    check.start = FALSE)
                    })
    out0 <- c(list(object), out0)
    # Need to add some error catching code. It is possible that all of them fail the check.
    fit_ok <- sapply(out0, lavaan::lavInspect, what = "post.check")
    out1 <- out0[fit_ok]
    fit_fmin <- sapply(out1, lavaan::fitMeasures, fit.measures = "fmin")
    out2 <- out1[which(fit_fmin == min(fit_fmin))]
    # Should add more diagnostic information
    out2[[1]]
  }

This function is certainly not yet ready for use (e.g., error checking need to be added, need a more robust way to change the starting values, etc.) but is sufficient to illustrate the idea, I think.

If the model does not take a long time to fit, maybe this can be done whenever a model is fitted, to check automatically whether the results are sensitive to the starting values.

If convergence failed, maybe this can also be done automatically to see if convergence can be achieved by changing the starting values.

Or, just like OpenMx, this can be a standalone function for users who would like to do this.

-- Shu Fai
